headline: 2027 memory manufacturing capacity reportedly sold out to AI companies
summary: A new report suggests Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron have pre-sold all DRAM and HBM capacity for 2027, primarily to AI firms, signaling continued price hikes for consumers.
details: A new report indicates that Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron have reportedly sold out their entire memory manufacturing capacity for 2027. This unprecedented demand is primarily driven by AI companies securing future supply.

According to Digitimes, all DRAM and HBM capacity for 2027 is now fully booked, with no further supply currently planned. While the manufacturers have not yet confirmed this, the report suggests significant implications for retail prices.

Many of these sales are through long-term purchasing agreements, effectively pre-ordering memory that hasn't even been produced yet over five-year terms. This trend makes it challenging to foresee an end to rising RAM prices and scarcity.

The impact extends beyond memory; NAND storage is also experiencing growing demand. Although NAND capacity isn't fully absorbed due to more suppliers, SSD prices have steadily increased over the past six months.

For example, the Western Digital SN7100 1TB SSD, a standard PCIe 4 drive, saw its price jump 52% from $110 in January to $189 currently. This illustrates the broader market pressure on storage components.

The ongoing memory crisis is already affecting other hardware, with recent price increases for the Xbox Series X and the Steam Machine. The high cost of memory is a significant factor across the tech industry.
